member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Behaviours.OrganizationAccessBehavior`2
member.summary: Checks before the handler runs. A caller who is not a member gets (404, so organization ids cannot be probed); a member whose role lacks the permission gets (403). Custom roles count with their own permission set. The resolved access is kept on for handlers that need it (member management). A request made with a storeasy token acts in the token's organization: the token's organization replaces the one in the request. A read only personal access token acts as a viewer (min of token and role). CI and upload tokens pass only requests marked (the handler limits them to their apps).

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Features.Account.GoogleSignIn.GoogleSignInCommandHandler
member.summary: Handles . Linking goes only by an address Google verified. When the existing account of that address was never verified (someone may have registered it without owning it), Google's proof takes it over: the address becomes verified, the unknown password is replaced with a random one (the owner can set a new one with "forgot password") and every session and token of the account ends. A new account gets a random password too, so it signs in with Google until its owner sets one. Locked accounts stay locked.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Features.AsoKeywords.ResearchAsoKeywords.ResearchAsoKeywordsCommand
member.summary: Queues the measurement of keywords for one app in one store and country from the store's public data (a job) and returns the job id at once: estimated popularity (the store's search autocomplete), difficulty (the strength of the first ten results), the number of competing apps, the top ten competitors, whether the app itself ranks, and an opportunity score. Store requests are paced, so measuring 20 new keywords takes a few minutes; read the progress and the result with GET aso-keywords/research. The same request while an identical job is still queued or running answers that job's id. Scores are estimates, never AI guesses. App Store and Google Play (competitors and rank on Play only when the operator enabled Play search pages); Microsoft Store is not supported. The public measurements are cached for every organization.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Features.MsStore.ApplyMsChange.ApplyMsChangeCommand
member.summary: Plans and, when asked, applies one Microsoft Store change: listings, images, MSIX packages (app or flight), price and availability, MSI/EXE installer packages, package rollout, a new flight, a new add-on, add-on content or discarding a draft. With (the default) only the plan comes back: diff, remarks, store calls, the permission applying needs and . Applying sends the same change with that hash; it is refused when the store content changed since, when the plan is blocked (single active submission, submission changed in Partner Center, Pricing Version 2, 409 products) or when the caller's role lacks the plan's permission. The write itself runs as a store job; submission edits stay in a draft until SubmitMsSubmission.

A plan that is not blocked is saved as a change plan of kind through : a dry run leaves it pending (approve it with the shared plan endpoints); applying approves it right away with the same rules (the plan's permission, a second store read through the Microsoft content gateway compared by fingerprint) and queues the job. member.summary: Makes an uploaded file (from POST organizations/logo/upload) the organization's logo, replacing the current one. member.summary: Handles . Pattern:
^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8}){0,2}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [a-z] greedily at least 2 and at most 3 times.
○ Loop greedily at most 2 times.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match '-'.
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit atomically at least 2 and at most 8 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Features.StoreConnections.ReplaceStoreConnectionKey.ReplaceStoreConnectionKeyCommand
member.summary: Replaces the key of an existing App Store Connect, Google Play or channel (winget and later) connection in place, so the connection id and everything linked to it (apps, jobs, history) stay. An Apple key must belong to the same team (the same issuer id); a Google service account may be another one; a channel's credential must be for the same account (the same winget-pkgs fork). The new key is checked offline, verified against the store and only then sealed in place of the old one; when verification fails the old key stays. A Microsoft secret is replaced with RotateMsConnectionSecretCommand.

member.name: P:Storeasy.Application.Features.StoreConnections.ReplaceStoreConnectionKey.ReplaceStoreConnectionKeyCommand.ConnectionId
member.summary: Apple, Google or channel connection.

member.name: P:Storeasy.Application.Features.StoreConnections.ReplaceStoreConnectionKey.ReplaceStoreConnectionKeyCommand.Secret
member.summary: The new secret JSON, in the shape the connection was added with. Apple: {"issuerId","keyId","privateKey"}. Google: the service account JSON key file content. winget: {"token","fork"}. Masked in logs.

member.name: P:Storeasy.Application.Features.StoreConnections.ReplaceStoreConnectionKey.ReplaceStoreConnectionKeyCommand.CredentialExpiryDate
member.summary: Expiry of the new credential, for stores that record one (a GitHub token); ignored otherwise.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Features.StoreConnections.ReplaceStoreConnectionKey.ReplaceStoreConnectionKeyCommandHandler
member.summary: Handles . The secret property is [LogMasked]. The new key is parsed with the same offline checks as adding a connection; an Apple key's issuer id is compared with the one sealed in the connection (opened in memory only for that); the key is verified against the store and only then sealed. The update writes the sealed secret, the fingerprint and the verification result in one statement, so a failure anywhere before it leaves the old key, fingerprint and status as they were.

member.summary: Handles the deletion of the user. A user who is the last owner of an organization is not deleted (409 naming the organizations: give them another owner first). Otherwise the user's organization memberships are removed with the user, the cached organization access goes, and the revocation stamp (which also closes the live connections) is rotated after the delete, so the deleted user's access tokens are rejected at once. member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.IAccountMailer
member.summary: Issues the one time account tokens and prepares the account e-mails (verification, password reset, invitation) in the current request culture. Nothing is sent on the request path: the mails go into the e-mail outbox () and a background sender delivers them, so the answer time of an anonymous endpoint does not depend on the provider or on whether an account exists. A failure to queue is logged and reported as false, never thrown, so the calling flow (registration, invitation) completes and the user can ask for the mail again.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.IMicrosoftStoreClient
member.summary: Typed client of the two Microsoft Store APIs: the MSIX submission API (manage.devcenter.microsoft.com: apps, app, flight and add-on submissions, package rollout) and the MSI/EXE submission API (api.store.microsoft.com: metadata, packages, readiness, submit). secretJson is the decrypted connection secret {"tenantId","clientId","clientSecret","sellerId"}; tokens are cached per connection until shortly before they expire. 429, 5xx and network failures are retried with backoff; failures surface as with a redacted message (409 is permanent and means the API refuses the product). Submissions are read and written as so that a PUT sends back every field the API returned.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore
member.summary: Per-user revocation stamp store. The stamp is the source of truth for "are this user's tokens still valid": it is baked into the access token at login and checked on every request. Backed by Redis for a cheap per-request read, with the database (User.SessionStamp) as the durable source of truth and a fail-safe fallback when Redis is unavailable.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.GetOrCreateAsync(System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Returns the user's current stamp, creating and persisting one if the user has none yet. Used when minting a token so the token always carries a valid stamp.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.RotateAsync(System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Rotates the user's stamp (new value persisted to the database and written through to the cache), instantly invalidating every access token that carried the old stamp. Called on password change, role change, lock and deletion. Call it after the transaction that revokes the sessions has committed (never inside it), so a concurrent request can never re-cache the old stamp.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.RotateManyAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.Int32},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Rotates the stamps of several users with one update (their access tokens stop working; a refresh issues new ones), for example when a global role they hold changed. Call it after the caller's transaction has committed.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.IsValidAsync(System.Int32,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Validates a stamp presented by a token against the user's current stamp (Redis, with a database fallback). Returns true when they match.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ITransactionRunner
member.summary:
Runs a unit of database work inside a real transaction that the transaction interceptor opens on the (proxied) implementation. Handlers use this to keep ONLY their DB mutations transactional while doing external work (cache writes, notifications, e-mail) AFTER the commit, instead of wrapping the whole handler in [Transaction] (which would drag those external calls inside the transaction).
Milvasoft interception is proxy-based, so the transaction only fires when the method is invoked through this injected interface. A private [Transaction] method on the handler itself would NOT open a transaction: a same-instance call bypasses the proxy (self-invocation), so the interceptor never runs.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ITransactionRunner.RunAsync(System.Func{System.Threading.Tasks.Task})
member.summary: Runs inside a transaction: commits when it completes, rolls back if it throws. Only put database mutations in ; do external calls after this returns.
member.param: The database work to run transactionally.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Analytics.AppleAnalyticsReports
member.summary:
The App Store Connect analytics reports storeasy reads (Analytics Reports API, standard content level, daily granularity) and their parsers. Files are tab separated with a header row.
"App Store Discovery and Engagement Standard" (category APP_STORE_ENGAGEMENT): Event Impression counts as impressions, Event Page view on a product page or store sheet as page views; by Source Type and Territory, summing Counts.
"App Downloads Standard" (category COMMERCE): Download Type First-time download counts as downloads, Redownload as redownloads (updates and restores are left out); by Source Type and Territory.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Analytics.PlayStatsReports
member.summary:
The Google Play Console statistics files storeasy reads from the developer's Cloud Storage bucket (gs://pubsite_prod_rev_...), one file per month and breakdown, UTF-16 comma separated with a header row:
stats/store_performance/store_performance_{package}_{yyyyMM}_country.csv: Date, Package name, Country, Store listing acquisitions, Store listing visitors, Store listing conversion rate. The totals come from here.
stats/store_performance/store_performance_{package}_{yyyyMM}_traffic_source.csv: Date, Package name, Traffic source, Search term, UTM source, UTM campaign and the same metrics. Rows are summed per day and source and only fill the source slices.
Store listing visitors are page views, store listing acquisitions are downloads; Play reports no impressions.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Analytics.ReportBuckets.BucketRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{1,220}[a-z0-9]$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [\-.0-9_a-z] greedily at least 1 and at most 220 times.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9a-z].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Analytics.StoreMetricAccumulator
member.summary: Sums store report facts into the daily slices of . A fact names its country and source when the report has that dimension (null when it does not); it is added to its own slice and to every coarser one: a fact of (TR, search) counts for (TR, search), (TR, all), (all, search) and (all, all). A fact that only a breakdown file carries (Google Play's traffic source file, while the country file holds the totals) is added with includeInTotal: false, so the total is not counted twice.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Aso.AsoCountries.CountryCode
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z]{2}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [a-z] exactly 2 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Aso.AsoCountries.LanguageCode
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Za-z]{2,3}([-_][A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match an ASCII letter greedily at least 2 and at most 3 times.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [\-_].
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit atomically at least 2 and at most 8 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Aso.AsoScoring
member.summary:
The ASO scores, computed only from what the stores return (never from a model). All are estimates on a 0 to 100 scale.
Popularity (): how early the store's own search autocomplete offers the keyword. The keyword is typed letter by letter in steps (, searched with a binary search); the shorter the prefix at which the keyword appears among the suggestions, and the higher it is listed there, the more people search it. 10 + 75 x ease + 15 x position, where ease is 1 when one letter is enough and 0 when only the whole keyword brings it, and position is 1 for the first suggestion. A keyword the autocomplete never offers scores 5 (other terms around it are searched) or 0 (nothing is).
Difficulty (): how strong the first ten search results are. 100 x (0.55 x ratings + 0.10 x stars + 0.20 x title match + 0.15 x crowding): ratings is the mean of log10(1 + rating count) / 5 capped at 1 (100,000 ratings count fully), stars the mean average rating / 5, title match the share of the ten whose name contains every word of the keyword, crowding the result count / 200 capped at 1.
Opportunity (): the geometric mean of popularity and ease (100 - difficulty), so a keyword needs both demand and room to score high.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Aso.ImpactMath
member.summary:
The arithmetic of the before and after impact report, without any I/O (docs/aso-impact.md):
Windows: the before window is the W days ending the day before the effect day; the after window is the W days starting gap days after the effect day (the default gap of 2 skips the effect day and the next, because stores apply changes with a delay).
Counts are compared as daily averages over the weekdays both windows have data for. With whole week windows (W a multiple of 7) and no missing day this is the plain daily average; otherwise a weekday present in one window only is left out of both, so a window with more weekend days does not look better or worse.
The conversion rate is total downloads over total page views of each window; its change is checked with a two proportion z-test. Below page views in a window or downloads in both, the signal is "not enough data".
Ranks are averaged over the checked days the app was in the results; a keyword ranked in one window only counts as improved (newly ranked) or declined (dropped out).

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Chrome.ChromeVersions.ItemIdRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-p]{32}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [a-p] exactly 32 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Chrome.ChromeVersions.PublisherIdRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 1 and at most 100 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Extensions.StoreasyExtensions.DataUriRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^data:(?<mediatype>[\w/+.-]+);base64,(?<data>[a-zA-Z0-9+/]+={0,2})$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "data:".
○ "mediatype" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+\--/\w] atomically at least once.
○ Match the string ";base64,".
○ "data" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+/-9A-Za-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match '=' atomically at most 2 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Extensions.StoreasyExtensions.ReplaceAndToLowerRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
\s+
Explanation:
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Extensions.StoreasyExtensions.UrlRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(ht|f)tp(s?)\:\/\/[0-9a-zA-Z]([-.\w]*[0-9a-zA-Z])*(:(0-9)*)*(\/?)([a-zA-Z0-9\-\.\?\,\'\/\\\+&%\$#_]*)?$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "ht".
○ Match 'f'.
○ Match the string "tp".
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match 's' atomically, optionally.
○ Match the string "://".
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [\-.\w] greedily any number of times.
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 4th capture group.
○ Match ':'.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 5th capture group.
○ Match the string "0-9".
○ 6th capture group.
○ Match '/' greedily, optionally.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 7th capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [#-'+-9?A-Z\\_a-z] atomically any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.CacheKeys
member.summary: Builds every Redis key of the application, always as {prefix}:{key} with the prefix of , so applications that share one Redis never read or overwrite each other's entries (revocation stamps, rate limit counters, the feature flag cache). The [Cache] interceptor gets the same prefix through its key configurator. A new Redis key is added here, never written as a literal at the call site.
member.remarks: A service that must reach another application's keys on purpose (an admin API that revokes the tokens of the main API's users) creates a second instance with that application's options instead of repeating the key format.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.GuidelineParser.GuidelineRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
Guideline\s+(?<code>\d+(?:\.\d+){0,3})(?:\s*\([a-z0-9]+\))*(?:[ \t]*[-:][ \t]*(?<title>[^\r\n]+))?
Options:
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase
Explanation:
○ Match a character in the set [Gg].
○ Match a character in the set [Uu].
○ Match a character in the set [Ii].
○ Match a character in the set [Dd].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Ll].
○ Match a character in the set [Ii].
○ Match a character in the set [Nn].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.
○ "code" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily at most 3 times.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match '('.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Za-z\u212A] atomically at least once.
○ Match ')'.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] atomically any number of times.
○ Match a character in the set [\-:].
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] greedily any number of times.
○ "title" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [^\n\r] atomically at least once.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor
member.summary: Removes anything that looks like a credential from text before it is logged, stored or returned: bearer tokens, JWTs, PEM private keys, Google access tokens, Apple webhook signatures, signed URL query strings and access_token query values (the SignalR websocket token), storeasy, GitHub and Anthropic tokens. Ported from store-ops redact().

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.BearerRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]+
Options:
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase
Explanation:
○ Match a character in the set [Bb].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Aa].
○ Match a character in the set [Rr].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Rr].
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.
○ Match a character in the set [+\--9=A-Z_a-z~\u212A] atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.JwtRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+
Explanation:
○ Match the string "eyJ".
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 8 times.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 8 times.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.PemRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]*?-----END [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----
Explanation:
○ Match the string "-----BEGIN ".
○ Match a character in the set [ A-Z] greedily any number of times.
○ Match the string "PRIVATE KEY-----".
○ Match any character lazily any number of times.
○ Match the string "-----END ".
○ Match a character in the set [ A-Z] greedily any number of times.
○ Match the string "PRIVATE KEY-----".

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.GoogleTokenRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
ya29\.[A-Za-z0-9._-]+
Explanation:
○ Match the string "ya29.".
○ Match a character in the set [\-.0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.AppleSignatureRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
hmacsha256=[0-9a-fA-F]+
Explanation:
○ Match the string "hmacsha256=".
○ Match a hexadecimal digit atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.AccessTokenQueryRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
access_token=[^&\s"']+
Options:
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase
Explanation:
○ Match a character in the set [Aa].
○ Match a character in the set [Cc] exactly 2 times.
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Ss] exactly 2 times.
○ Match '_'.
○ Match a character in the set [Tt].
○ Match a character in the set [Oo].
○ Match a character in the set [Kk\u212A].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Nn].
○ Match '='.
○ Match a character in the set [^"&'\s] atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.SignedUrlRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
(https://[^\s"'?]+)\?[^\s"']*(?:Signature|signature|X-Amz|sig=|token=|access_token=)[^\s"']*
Explanation:
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match the string "https://".
○ Match a character in the set [^"'?\s] atomically at least once.
○ Match '?'.
○ Match a character in the set [^"'\s] greedily any number of times.
○ Match with 6 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "Signature".
○ Match the string "signature".
○ Match the string "X-Amz".
○ Match the string "sig=".
○ Match the string "token=".
○ Match the string "access_token=".
○ Match a character in the set [^"'\s] atomically any number of times.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.StoreasyTokenRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
\b(?<kind>sea|sci|sut|whsec)_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}
Explanation:
○ Match if at a word boundary.
○ "kind" capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match 's'.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "ea".
○ Match the string "ci".
○ Match the string "ut".
○ Match the string "whsec".
○ Match '_'.
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 8 times.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.SecretRedactor.GitHubTokenRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
\u0008(?<kind>gh[pousr]|github_pat)_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}
Explanation:
○ Match '\b'.
○ "kind" capture group.
○ Match 'g'.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match 'h'.
○ Match a character in the set [oprsu].
○ Match the string "ithub_pat".
○ Match '_'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 8 times.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.UserUniqueConstraintHelper
member.summary: Maps a unique-index violation on Users to the message key the pre-insert checks would have returned. The check-then-insert in CreateUser is racy by nature: two requests can pass the "is this username taken?" query at the same time and only the database can reject the second one (23505). Without this, that loser gets a generic "duplicate data" answer instead of "this username is already taken".

member.summary: Whether (or its inner exception, as EF wraps it) is a unique violation (23505) of the index . For set based updates (ExecuteUpdateAsync) that race on a unique column outside the user table, e.g. an organization slug; this class is the one place the application layer reads Npgsql.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Monetization.MonetizationPlanner
member.summary: Turns requested monetization changes into a change plan, purely: every change is checked against the store's current products (), becomes field level items (before and after), the store calls the apply job will make, warnings, and an operation completed with the store's ids. The plan needs the highest permission of its items: a price change of a product on sale needs and, when it reaches existing subscribers, a typed confirmation. storeasy never computes a price: App Store prices are price points (equalized by the store), Play prices are what the member entered or Play converted.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Monetization.MonetizationPlanner.PlanIdPattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9a-z] atomically at most 62 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Monetization.MonetizationPlanner.IsoPeriodPattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^P(\d+[YMWD])+$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match 'P'.
○ Loop atomically at least once.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match a character in the set [DMWY].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Winget.WingetCredentialParser.TokenRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,250}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,250})$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match 'g'.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "hp_".
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit atomically at least 30 and at most 250 times.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "ithub_pat_".
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 30 and at most 250 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Winget.WingetCredentialParser.ForkRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9]|-(?=[A-Za-z0-9])){0,38}/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit.
○ Loop greedily at most 38 times.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '-'.
○ Zero-width positive lookahead.
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit.
○ Match '/'.
○ Match a character in the set [\-.0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 1 and at most 100 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Winget.WingetFields.PackageIdentifier
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[^\.\s\\/:\*\?"<>\|\x01-\x1f]{1,32}(\.[^\.\s\\/:\*\?"<>\|\x01-\x1f]{1,32}){1,7}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [^\u0001-\u001F"*./:<>?\\|\s] atomically at least 1 and at most 32 times.
○ Loop greedily at least 1 and at most 7 times.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [^\u0001-\u001F"*./:<>?\\|\s] atomically at least 1 and at most 32 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Winget.WingetFields.PackageVersion
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[^\\/:\*\?"<>\|\x01-\x1f]+$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [^\u0001-\u001F"*/:<>?\\|] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Winget.WingetFields.Locale
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^([a-zA-Z]{2,3}|[iI]-[a-zA-Z]+|[xX]-[a-zA-Z]{1,8})(-[a-zA-Z]{1,8})*$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match an ASCII letter greedily at least 2 and at most 3 times.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Ii].
○ Match '-'.
○ Match an ASCII letter greedily at least once.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Xx].
○ Match '-'.
○ Match an ASCII letter greedily at least 1 and at most 8 times.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '-'.
○ Match an ASCII letter atomically at least 1 and at most 8 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Winget.WingetFields.Sha256
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Fa-f0-9]{64}$
Explanation:

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Winget.WingetFields.Url
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^([Hh][Tt][Tt][Pp][Ss]?)://.+$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [Hh].
○ Match a character in the set [Tt] exactly 2 times.
○ Match a character in the set [Pp].
○ Match a character in the set [Ss] atomically, optionally.
○ Match the string "://".
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
